What Is Gynecomastia? Male Breast Enlargement Explained by a Plastic Surgeon

By Dr. M. Ram Prabhu · 22 May 2026 · 10 min read

Gynecomastia is enlargement of male breast tissue. It is common, but many boys and men feel embarrassed to talk about it because it affects confidence in shirts, gyms, swimming pools, and social situations.

This article expands on Dr. Ram Prabhu's Telugu educational video about gynecomastia, also called male breast enlargement.

What gynecomastia means

Gynecomastia is enlargement of glandular tissue behind the nipple in males. It may happen on one side or both sides. In many patients, the enlarged gland is also mixed with fat.

The typical finding is a firm or rubbery glandular disc behind the nipple. The nipple may look puffy or project forward through a T-shirt.

Why it happens

Gynecomastia can happen because of hormonal imbalance, especially relatively higher estrogen effect or lower testosterone effect. Puberty is a common time for this to appear.

Other causes can include certain medicines, supplements, anabolic steroids, medical conditions, or weight gain. In many patients, no single clear trigger is found.

Symptoms and confidence issues

Gynecomastia can cause:

  • Chest enlargement
  • Puffy nipples
  • Tenderness or shock-like pain in some patients
  • Embarrassment while wearing fitted T-shirts
  • Avoidance of swimming, gym, or shirtless situations
  • Reduced confidence

The emotional effect is real. A condition that looks small to others may feel very heavy to the person living with it.

Can exercise or medicines reduce gynecomastia?

Exercise can build chest muscle. Weight loss can reduce fat. But a firm gland behind the nipple usually does not disappear with exercise alone.

If the problem is only fat, weight reduction may help. But true gynecomastia with glandular tissue often needs surgical correction when it persists and bothers the patient.

How gynecomastia is diagnosed

In most cases, gynecomastia is a clinical diagnosis. A plastic surgeon examines the chest, checks the gland, fat, skin, nipple position, and asymmetry.

Hormonal tests may be advised in selected cases, especially if there are signs of ongoing hormonal imbalance such as delayed beard growth, lack of underarm hair, or other endocrine symptoms.

Treatment overview

For persistent gynecomastia, surgery is often the definitive option. Modern treatment is usually minimally invasive, using small access points to remove fat and gland.

Many patients are treated as day-care cases, meaning they come in the morning and go home the same day. Return to light work can be early, but gym and chest-loading exercises are restarted only after clearance.

For full planning, read the main gynecomastia surgery page, the cost guide, and the recovery timeline.

Video transcript: English version edited for readability

Dr. Ram Prabhu introduces himself as a plastic surgeon and explains that gynecomastia means male breast enlargement. It is commonly seen in young boys and men. Although common, it can be embarrassing, and many patients hesitate to talk about it.

He explains that patients may feel shy removing their shirt, going to the swimming pool, going to the gym, or wearing T-shirts because the chest enlargement becomes visible. This can reduce confidence.

The common causes include hormonal imbalance: increased estrogen effect or reduced testosterone effect. Certain drugs and medicines may also contribute.

The main physical finding is firm glandular tissue behind the nipple. It may be associated with fat. Some patients have enlargement on one side; many have it on both sides.

Gynecomastia can cause chest enlargement, tenderness, shock-like pain on touch in some patients, and loss of confidence. A common question is whether exercise or medicines can reduce it. Dr. Ram Prabhu explains that exercise can grow the chest muscle, and weight loss can reduce fat, but the gland usually does not shrink with exercise.

Some patients ask whether they have gynecomastia or only fat. Every male has a small breast gland from birth. Whether it is enlarged or not is best assessed by a plastic surgeon. Only fat without gland is less common, and when it is only fat, weight reduction may help.

When gynecomastia does not reduce with medicines or exercise, surgery is an option. The surgery can be minimally invasive, using small holes to remove fat and gland. It is usually a day-care procedure, and many patients can return to work or college early.

Diagnosis is usually clinical. The surgeon examines chest enlargement, firm tissue behind the nipple, and puffy nipple appearance. In rare cases with signs of excess estrogen or hormonal imbalance, hormone testing may be advised.

FAQ

Is gynecomastia common?

Yes. It is common, especially around puberty, but persistent gynecomastia can continue into adulthood.

Can gym workouts remove gynecomastia?

Workouts can build muscle and reduce fat, but they usually cannot remove firm glandular tissue behind the nipple.

How do I know if it is fat or gland?

A plastic surgeon can examine the chest and identify whether the enlargement is gland, fat, skin excess, or a combination.
